cards.front: Within 72 hours of a sensitising event, offer [___].
cards.context:
After a sensitising bleed, anti-D binds fetal cells before the mother starts her own immune response.

Offer it within 72 hours, and do not delay if the woman is in front of you.

cards.front: Intestinal obstruction can increase neonatal unconjugated bilirubin through increased [___].
cards.context:
Slow intestinal transit permits bilirubin deconjugation and reabsorption, increasing the unconjugated fraction. Intestinal obstruction differs from biliary obstruction, which causes conjugated jaundice.

Examples include pyloric stenosis, meconium ileus, duodenal atresia and Hirschsprung disease. Poor intake can also contribute; investigate the obstruction rather than assuming physiological jaundice.

cards.front: Bedside features split antepartum haemorrhage: a [___] uterus with painless bleeding suggests a low-segment placenta; a hard/woody uterus with painful bleeding suggests abruption. Speculum + urgent USS go first; digital vaginal exam is deferred until imaging excludes a low-segment implantation.
cards.context:
The two major causes of antepartum haemorrhage have opposing bedside signatures: placenta praevia (painless, soft uterus, often recurrent) versus abruption (painful, tense/woody uterus, fetal distress).

Workup is speculum + urgent USS first — digital vaginal exam is catastrophic if praevia is present and undiagnosed.

cards.front: Postpartum endometritis risk is increased after [___]; an IV regimen for severe/systemic infection is amoxicillin + gentamicin + metronidazole.
cards.context:
Caesarean birth increases the risk of postpartum endometritis. Fever, uterine tenderness and offensive lochia suggest infection; assess for sepsis and retained products.

SA Health recommends IV amoxicillin, gentamicin and metronidazole for severe/systemic endometritis; metronidazole forms DNA-damaging radicals in anaerobes. Allergy and local protocols determine alternatives.

[RANZCOG review](https://www.ogmagazine.org.au/21/4-21/managing-the-septic-postnatal-patient/).

cards.front: In normal pregnancy, the total red cell mass [___].
cards.context: Plasma volume rises proportionally more than red cell mass, so the haemoglobin concentration falls even though red cell mass increases — a dilutional effect, not true iron deficiency (though that can coexist).

cards.front: The combined oral contraceptive pill works mainly by suppressing [___].
cards.context:
The pill combines estrogen and progestogen to prevent the ovarian release of an egg. It also thickens cervical mucus.

For standard ethinylestradiol pills, starting active pills on menstrual days 1–5 gives immediate protection; later starts need seven days of backup. Other formulations have separate instructions.

cards.front: In placenta accreta spectrum, the deepest subtype — villi penetrate through the serosa and may invade bladder or bowel — is [___].
cards.context:
PAS is abnormal placentation: chorionic villi invade beyond the decidua basalis (deficient over a prior scar), so the placenta cannot separate at delivery.

Depth grades the invasion — accreta attaches to the myometrium, increta invades into it, percreta penetrates through the serosa. See the table and A-I-P mnemonic below.

cards.front: The plate on the anterior side of the large soft gap, with a paired plate across the midline, is the [___].
cards.context: The plate lies on the anterior side of the large soft gap, with a paired plate across the midline. That anterior plate is the frontal bone.

cards.front: Under the 2025 ADIPS criteria, gestational diabetes (GDM) diagnostic thresholds on 75g OGTT are: fasting ≥[___], 1-hour ≥10.6, or 2-hour ≥9.0 mmol/L.
cards.context:
One value at or above any threshold is enough to diagnose GDM. The 2025 values sit where HAPO found the odds of a large, hyperinsulinaemic baby were twice those at the average glucose.

ADIPS 2025 replaced the 2014 values (5.1 / 10.0 / 8.5), which sat at 1.75 times those odds. NSW Health notified services in August 2025, so older questions may differ.

cards.front: [___] is the first-line treatment for eclamptic seizures (superior to diazepam and phenytoin). Loading dose: 4g IV over 15–20 minutes.
cards.context:
Magnesium sulfate is first-line for eclamptic seizure treatment AND prevention in severe pre-eclampsia.

Mechanism is multifactorial: NMDA antagonism, cerebral vasodilation and neuroprotection. It beat diazepam and phenytoin in eclampsia (Collaborative Eclampsia Trial); Magpie halved eclampsia against placebo.

Loading dose: 4 g IV over 15-20 minutes, then 1 g/hour for 24 hours post-delivery or last seizure. Watch for toxicity (loss of patellar reflexes first, then respiratory depression) — antidote is IV calcium gluconate.

cards.front: In a woman with postmenopausal bleeding who is not taking hormone therapy, endometrial thickness greater than [___] on transvaginal ultrasound warrants endometrial sampling.
cards.context:
This threshold applies to postmenopausal bleeding. Persistent or recurrent bleeding, poor visualisation or cancer risk factors can warrant sampling despite a thin endometrium.

Office biopsy may sample diffuse disease; hysteroscopy assesses focal lesions or an inadequate sample. Hormone-therapy bleeding needs regimen-specific assessment.

cards.front: Absence of one paramesonephric duct, which would have built one tube and half the uterine body, leaves a [___] uterus.
cards.context:
The paramesonephric ducts are paired. Each one makes a uterine tube and half the uterine body, so a duct that never forms leaves that side absent.

The remaining duct still builds one tube and one horn. That pattern is a unicornuate uterus, not a failure of fusion.

cards.front: Outpatient pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) empirical antibiotics: ceftriaxone (gonorrhoea) + doxycycline (chlamydia) + [___] (anaerobes).
cards.context:
PID is polymicrobial (Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, Mycoplasma genitalium, anaerobes); empirical antibiotics must cover all: ceftriaxone (gonorrhoea) + doxycycline (chlamydia) + metronidazole (anaerobes).

Threshold to treat is deliberately low (CDC): any sexually active woman with pelvic pain + cervical motion tenderness OR uterine tenderness OR adnexal tenderness — start treatment.

Most managed as outpatients (oral, review at 72 h); admit for IV if pregnant, severe, suspected tubo-ovarian abscess, no response to oral, or unable to tolerate oral. Sexual partner notification + treatment essential.

cards.front: A woman with a previous unprovoked deep vein thrombosis received LMWH through pregnancy and has now given birth. To prevent venous thromboembolism, she should continue LMWH for at least [___].
cards.context:
Thrombotic risk is highest in the weeks after birth. A woman with a previous venous thromboembolism is high risk.

High-risk women continue low molecular weight heparin for 6 weeks after birth; lower-risk women need shorter courses.

cards.front: Outpatient pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) empirical antibiotics: ceftriaxone (gonorrhoea) + [___] (chlamydia) + metronidazole (anaerobes).
cards.context:
PID is polymicrobial (Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, Mycoplasma genitalium, anaerobes); empirical antibiotics must cover all: ceftriaxone (gonorrhoea) + doxycycline (chlamydia) + metronidazole (anaerobes).

Threshold to treat is deliberately low (CDC): any sexually active woman with pelvic pain + cervical motion tenderness OR uterine tenderness OR adnexal tenderness — start treatment.

Most managed as outpatients (oral, review at 72 h); admit for IV if pregnant, severe, suspected tubo-ovarian abscess, no response to oral, or unable to tolerate oral. Sexual partner notification + treatment essential.

cards.front: Ligating the uterine artery beside the cervix can crush the [___], because the artery winds superior and anterior to it.
cards.context:
The uterine artery passes superior and anterior to the ureter as it reaches the cervix. Ligating the artery there can include the ureter in the clamp.

A different danger point is the pelvic brim, where the ovarian vessels are ligated at oophorectomy. That is not the cervical pedicle.

cards.front: Placental abruption is diagnosed clinically; ultrasound detects only about [___] of cases, so a normal scan does not exclude it.
cards.context:
The diagnostic trap is concealed abruption: blood may dissect between placenta and uterine wall WITHOUT escaping through the cervix.

A woman with severe pain and a tender, 'wooden' uterus can have little or no visible vaginal bleeding.

Risk factors cluster around vascular insult: prior abruption (5-15% recurrence), pre-eclampsia, smoking, cocaine, blunt trauma, IUGR, advanced age, IVF, multiparity.

cards.front: A woman with HIV has taken antiretroviral therapy throughout pregnancy, and her viral load is under 50 copies/mL at 36 weeks. With no obstetric indication for caesarean, the recommended mode of birth is [___].
cards.context:
On effective antiretroviral therapy with a viral load under 50 copies/mL near term, vaginal birth carries no added transmission risk, so caesarean offers no benefit.

Planned caesarean is considered when the viral load near birth is detectable or unknown. With suppression, perinatal transmission is about 0.1%.

cards.front: The newborn resuscitation set is prepared for [___].
cards.context:
A normal antenatal course and a normal heart-rate trace do not guarantee a smooth transition. Only a small share of babies need ventilation, and some of those births looked low risk.

The set is therefore opened for every birth. Calling an advanced life support clinician is a separate choice, made when the birth is high risk.

cards.front: Chlamydia testing, whether prompted by symptoms or screening, uses a [___] test on an appropriate specimen.
cards.context:
Chlamydia is often silent, so screening matters; dysuria, discharge or pelvic pain can also prompt testing. Untreated infection can cause pelvic inflammatory disease and later tubal complications.

For women not having a speculum examination, a self-collected vaginal swab is preferred. First-pass urine is used in men or when a vaginal or endocervical swab cannot be obtained; it is less sensitive in women.

cards.front: The key bedside test in a jittery, poorly-feeding at-risk newborn is a blood [___].
cards.context:
Neonatal hypoglycaemia is often non-specific (jittery, poor feeding, lethargy, seizures).

So the at-risk baby (preterm, SGA/LGA, infant of a diabetic mother) needs a low threshold to check — the bedside glucose is the key test.

cards.front: NSW usually collects newborn [___] screening at 48-72 hours of age.
cards.context:
The newborn screen needs the baby to have fed, and some analytes are unreliable in the first day of life.

NSW collects the blood spot at 48 to 72 hours.

cards.front: Fetal breech presentation increases the risk of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH); the reduced-amniotic-fluid condition linked with it is [___].
cards.context:
Breech, female sex, family history and oligohydramnios increase DDH risk ([meta-analysis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39853978/)).

Prematurity alone is not an established risk factor ([review](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12887-023-04083-1)).

cards.front: APH is bleeding from the genital tract from 20+0 weeks until birth; affects [___]% of pregnancies; never perform digital VE until praevia excluded.
cards.context:
The 20-week threshold separates APH from threatened miscarriage. Australian guidelines count bleeding up to the birth; some sources stop at the onset of labour.

Two safety rules drive the workup. First, stabilise the mother before chasing the cause: large-bore access, FBC + coag + group-and-hold, fetal assessment, and anti-D if Rh-negative.

Second, no digital vaginal exam until ultrasound has excluded placenta praevia — probing a low-lying placenta can provoke catastrophic haemorrhage.

cards.front: USS signs of placenta accreta spectrum include loss of retroplacental clear zone, placental [___] (Swiss cheese), bladder wall interruption, and myometrial thinning.
cards.context:
Antenatal USS signs of PAS are specific rather than sensitive. Loss of the retroplacental clear zone is about 66% sensitive and 96% specific; placental lacunae ('Swiss cheese') about 77% and 95%.

MRI is added for inconclusive USS or to map percreta extent (especially bladder/bowel invasion); USS sensitivity for PAS is ~80-90% in expert hands.

cards.front: Preterm birth is birth between 20+0 and [___]+6 weeks; affects ~8-9% of Australian pregnancies and is the leading cause of mortality in children <5.
cards.context:
Gestation is written weeks+days, so 20+0 = 20 weeks 0 days and 36+6 = the last day before 37 weeks (term); the 20-week floor is the same threshold that separates preterm birth from miscarriage.

Sub-categorised by severity: late preterm (34-36+6, ~70% of cases, generally good outcomes), moderate (32-33+6), very preterm (28-31+6, significant NICU need), and extremely preterm (<28 weeks).

Even late preterm infants have higher rates of learning difficulties, ADHD, and reduced educational attainment than term peers — which is why prevention matters even near term.
